parsed_reminder:
The memory bank status indicates the double-destruction theory has been **ruled out** - shutdown() has proper guards (null-check at line 175, sets pointer to nullptr at line 178). The re-examination in Step 10 confirmed this.

The actual issue identified: Static C++ standard library objects are being allocated from the custom heap (after it's activated at line 149) but then destroyed during program teardown **after** the custom heap has been cleaned up. This causes a crash when those static destructors try to free memory that wasn't allocated via regular malloc.

The fix approach: In user_init() (which is called at line 146, **before** the custom heap is set up at line 149), trigger initialization of stdlib features so their static objects use regular malloc instead of the custom heap. This ensures proper cleanup order.

Next action should be implementing this fix in /app/user.cpp, not re-investigating the shutdown mechanism.
